title: Reachability from a guarded single step
statement: Fix a finite nondeterministic Boolean machine, a computation mode, an input word $y$, a register bound $B$, labels $l,l'$, and register assignments $v,v'$. If the configuration at label $l$ with registers $v$ satisfies the guard—that is, its instruction meets the required preconditions and every register is at most $B$—and one computation step takes it to label $l'$ with registers $v'$, then that endpoint is reachable from the initial configuration $(l,v)$ while the guard holds at every earlier step.
hypotheses_covered: The starting configuration $(l,v)$ satisfies the reachability guard
One computation step takes $(l,v)$ at label $l$ to $(l',v')$
